title: Why Does the Universe Look Built for Us?
question: The physical constants of our universe sit in an improbably narrow range that allows stars, chemistry, and life to exist at all — is that a mystery demanding an explanation, or a mistake of perspective?
summary: Small changes to fundamental constants like the strength of gravity or the nuclear force would leave a universe with no stars, no carbon, and no observers to notice. This apparent fine-tuning has three very different families of explanation on offer — multiverse, selection effect, or design — each with real scientific and philosophical costs.
